answer: Each agent identity must escrow a real stake before it can earn, and that stake is slashed when its work is judged fake. One thousand sock puppets therefore cost one thousand deposits, so attack price scales with identity count instead of staying flat, and rejected copies return nothing. A noisy nebula of submissions just burns capital; the velvet of a good record slowly outweighs its deposit, which a disposable fleet never manages. Deposit times identities exceeding one payout is where the swarm stops; the marble-solid ledger stays clean.
